newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo AIDS drug shows promise against hepatitis.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo AIDS drug shows promise against hepatitis.

text.p: Pharmaceuticals giant Glaxo Wellcome said Thursday a drug originally developed for use against the virus that causes AIDS had shown promising results against hepatitis.
Glaxo said its drug lamivudine worked well in clinical trials with patients who had severe liver disease caused by hepatitis B.
Lamivudine, also known as 3TC, is already sold for use against AIDS under the brand name Epivir.
Glaxo said its hepatitis study involved 358 Asian patients with chronic hepatitis B in Hong Kong, Singapore and Taiwan.
Lamivudine was developed by BioChem Pharma Inc. in Canada and was licensed to Glaxo in 1990.
Analysts' estimates on the drug's sales prospects vary widely, ranging from a potential 200 million British pounds ($324.6 million) a year to more than 1 billion pounds ($1.62 billion).

But they say it will be hard to market lamivudine as only 2 percent of hepatitis B sufferers live in the developed world. The World Health Organisation estimates that around 350 million people carry the hepatitis B virus worldwide.
Hepatitis B is 100 times more infectious than HIV and can lead to severe liver scarring. It is responsible for 80 percent of cases of liver cancer.
